claims.statement: CMR governs liability and compensation for loss, damage, or delay, while eCMR supplies electronic proof of pickup and delivery.
Demand hypothesis: insurers and TMS channels will pay for evidence completeness because cargo policies require loss notification and supporting documentation.

contrary_evidence: eCMR platforms may add claim capture natively.
Cargo claims are infrequent for many fleets.

economics.acquisition_route: Partner with one eCMR or TMS vendor and one cargo broker.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 250000 monthly shipments across embedded channels can create 6 million PLN annual platform revenue and founder equity above 5 million PLN in five years.
economics.founder_time: Four hours daily for integrations and evidence-rule tuning.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 80-90% margin after automated capture and document assembly.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 25000 shipments monthly at 2 PLN cover initial capital within eighteen months.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 1-4 PLN per shipment plus 100-400 PLN per submitted claim pack.
economics.retention_or_repeat: The capture workflow runs on every shipment even when claims are rare.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Lane, carrier, damage-type, and claim-outcome data improve evidence prompts and triage.
fingerprint.customer: Road carriers, freight forwarders, cargo owners, and marine or cargo insurers.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: TMS and eCMR providers embed it at driver handoff and insurer notification.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: The workflow binds signed eCMR events, photos, reservations, sensor logs, and policy data into FNOL evidence.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A TMS provider, broker, insurer, or carrier pays per shipment and claim pack.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Damage, shortage, loss, or delay is discovered at handoff and proof is scattered across drivers and systems.

founder_fit: Evidence automation fits the founder's data background.
A software channel avoids camera exposure and manual claims handling.
risks: Insurer-specific requirements may create costly fragmentation.

structure.control_point: The signed chain-of-custody and exception record.
structure.critical_dependency: Driver adoption and insurer acceptance of digital evidence.

thesis: An eCMR-native relay can preserve pickup, delivery, exception, image, and sensor evidence and submit a clean cargo-loss notification.
title: eCMR Cargo Claim Evidence Relay
uncertainties: Per-shipment willingness to pay is untested.
The best initial payer among TMS, broker, and insurer is unknown.
